title: Backroom A+B — actionable outstanding research by specific problem (not mixed status flags)
notes: All 71 nonduplicate flagged records assigned exactly ONE primary actionable research group.
Each record has a plain-English issue and a targeted research task; secondary tags retain other concerns.
Eight definitively identified duplicate candidate records were removed in previous clean-up; not included in these 71.
Four demonstrably obsolete/unsafe sites are in automatic-exclusion group A; source evidence is preserved.
The 131 mapped Hold candidates remain in the other clean research file; this document covers flagged issues, not all 202 nonduplicate records.
Research categories are based on the saved evidence; they are not newly verified web claims.

groups.name: Confirmed obsolete, closed or unusable
groups.what_this_means: The original site has been demolished, converted, or is an unsafe derelict property. There is no current usable cruising site in this record.
groups.search_instruction: Exclude these from new active cruising entries now. Preserve historical evidence; only reinstate on credible evidence that a new, accessible cruising site exists.

examples.name: Jerma Palace Glory Hole
examples.problem: Jerma Palace is a derelict unsafe site; no operating public WC or current activity was established.
examples.research: Determine whether any operating lawful public facility replaced the former Jerma Palace site; the original derelict property should not be listed.

examples.name: Karlshorst Treskowallee
examples.problem: The old facility at Karlshorst Treskowallee was reported demolished and closed.
examples.research: Confirm that the former Karlshorst Treskowallee facility was demolished and archive the obsolete location.

examples.name: Wetherspoons Pub in The Capitol
examples.problem: The Capitol Wetherspoons pub closed in 2023 and the property changed to a children's soft-play business.
examples.research: Archive the Wetherspoons Capitol listing: the pub closed in 2023 and the property was converted to children's soft play in 2026.

groups.name: Might be closed, rebuilt or temporarily inaccessible
groups.what_this_means: An identified place has a dated closure, construction, sealed entrance, or uncertain reopening.
groups.search_instruction: Search current operator, municipal, road authority, Google Maps and recent dated firsthand reports to establish whether the ORIGINAL facility reopened, was replaced, or is still unavailable.

groups.what_this_means: The site can be identified, but official access, private property, safety, or opening-hour constraints undermine the directory claim.
groups.search_instruction: Find official access rules and independently dated safety/current-use evidence. Do not recommend restricted property or infer permission to cruise from general public access.

groups.search_instruction: Inspect the original source map, photos, replies and other cruising directories for a real place name, address or landmark. If none can be established, mark insufficient identity—not merely missing GPS.
